sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very close to I. minitabundus and I. severus. Soldier medium- to large-sized, on average slightly larger than I. severus; left mandible slightly curved to almost straight, clearly less curved than the right (as in I. minitabundus), but the left-right asymmetry is greater than in I. severus: ratio of the minor curvature of the left mandible to that of the right 0.68—1.02 (I. minitabundus 0.51—1.03, I. severus 0.79—1.24). The head is usually markedly domed (as in I. severus and in I. bulbifrons, which has the finitimus-type enteric valve). Worker medium- to large-sized, the enteric valve of the fungifaber type, in about 6% of samples intermediate between the fungifaber and finitimus types; the premolar of the left mandible more distinct than in most species (as in I. severus and I. minitabundus). Alate medium- to large-sized, the premolar of the left mandible likewise distinct; that revision established 4 subspecies on the basis of body size (first principal component) and the dimensions of the compound eyes and ocelli (second principal component), of which the nominal subspecies is one.

note: Adapted from the species-level diagnosis in the revision by Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the measurement abbreviations and ratios have been replaced by descriptive Chinese names. The original establishes 4 subspecies for this species; this entry records only the diagnostic characters of the species and does not set out the differences between subspecies.
